claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced high-temperature plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced high-temperature toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Chemical disorder in WTaTiVZr produces lattice distortion and local stress fields.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr increases dislocation cross-slip at elevated temperatures.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes dynamic recovery and dislocation annihilation at elevated temperatures.
The multiple principal elements in WTaTiVZr lower the energy barriers for dislocation movement at elevated temperatures through lattice-strain effects.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and recovery produce a more homogeneous distribution of plastic strain in WTaTiVZr.
More uniform dislocation motion and dynamic recovery blunt crack tips.
Crack-tip blunting delays crack initiation and propagation, thereby enhancing toughness.
At 800–1200 °C under matched loading conditions, WTaTiVZr will have higher strain to failure than pure tungsten.
At 800–1200 °C under matched loading conditions, WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before fracture than pure tungsten.
At 800–1200 °C under matched loading conditions, crack propagation will be delayed in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Post-test WTaTiVZr will exhibit a more dispersed dislocation structure than pure tungsten.
Post-test WTaTiVZr will show more evidence of dynamic recovery than pure tungsten.
The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism is expected to dominate between 800 and 1200 °C at strain rates typical of plasma-facing-component operation.
The proposed mechanism may be less significant at lower temperatures or under static conditions because lattice-distortion effects are less activated.
Matching grain size, geometry, temperature, strain rate, and loading mode between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten provides a controlled comparison of their high-temperature responses.

A lack of statistically significant improvements in both strain to failure and toughness, together with similar dislocation and crack-propagation behavior, would falsify the proposed primary mechanism.
